You honestly sound like you have the hardest part figured out already... retention and client experience. A lot of med spas can get leads, but very few can get people to come back over and over. That tells me your issue probably is not your service quality. It is likely visibility, positioning, and conversion systems.

One thing I see constantly with med spas in that 2-5 year stage is they rely heavily on:
• boosted posts  
• generic Meta ads  
• Google ads with no real nurture system  
• random specials that attract price shoppers  

Instead of building a true referral and community engine.

A few things that are working really well right now for smaller owner-led practices:

• Partnership marketing  
Partner with gyms, hormone clinics, hair salons, wellness providers, bridal vendors, women’s boutiques, fitness studios, etc. Not just leaving cards... actual co-hosted events, email swaps, VIP nights, referral perks.

• Client journey follow up  
Most spas lose money after the consult. Speed to lead, follow up, rebooking, memberships, package conversations, birthday/reactivation campaigns matter more than most owners realize.

• Educational content over promotional content  
People are exhausted by “$9.99 Botox Day” marketing. The spas winning right now feel personal, trustworthy, educational, and lifestyle driven. Especially for women 35+.

• Before & after storytelling  
Not just photos. Talk about confidence, hormones, aging gracefully, skin journeys, busy moms wanting to feel like themselves again. Emotion converts more than discounts.

• Small intimate events  
The giant open house model is getting tired unless you already have a huge database. Smaller “girls night” style events with one focused topic tend to convert much better.

• Google reviews + local SEO  
If your current clients love you, this is gold. Most happy clients simply never get asked to leave reviews consistently. Google still matters massively for med spas.

Also... and this is important... a lot of spas think they have a lead problem when they actually have a visibility and conversion problem. I’ve seen practices double revenue without increasing ad spend just by tightening up consult flow, offers, memberships, follow up, and retention systems.

You’re definitely not alone in this. The industry is noisy right now and a lot of owners are feeling this exact pressure. But the good news is loyal clients usually mean the foundation is strong.

Answer this FB post: Hello everyone!!  I am an Advanced Esthetician/ Med Spa owner in Southern Oregon.  I have a collaborative agreement and a medical director.  We offer advanced aesthetics and weight loss.  I have been open for 2.5 years.  We are struggling to find new clients.  Our current clients are loyal, love our services and keep returning.  What types of marketing, events, specials, networking or other ideas have you done that have gotten good returns.  Wanting to grow and help more people and just can't seem to find them.  We have a google based website and sponsored google ads.  We also run some Meta ads.  Any advice is welcome!
Make it much shorter and offer to help her get clarity if she wants

Honestly, if your current clients are loyal and keep coming back, that’s a really good sign. Usually that means the issue is not your services, it’s visibility, positioning, or conversion systems.

A lot of med spas are struggling right now because they’re relying on generic ads and promos instead of building strong referral systems, partnerships, follow-up, memberships, and educational content that actually connects emotionally with women.

Most of the time it’s not a lead problem... it’s a systems and messaging problem.

I’d be happy to help you get some clarity on where the gaps might be if you want another set of eyes on it 😊
